svg.title: DDIA 14 · DOING THE RIGHT THING: sketchnote
svg.text: Data is often about people. Engineers share responsibility
for what systems decide about them and collect about them.
Deciding about a person, not the weather
Unsure? The rational corporate answer is "no"
No proof, no trial, often no appeal
Models learn bias from past decisions
Removing race is not enough: postcode is a
Predictions are right on average, wrong for
Who answers for the algorithm's mistake?
Missed payments → lower score → no job → worse finances →
lower score. Systems thinking: does it amplify or counter
Logging behaviour as a side effect changes
Consent is weak: opaque, one-sided, costly to
Privacy = the right to decide what to reveal
data you don't have can't leak
all inherit what you store. Treat users as
Log only fields with a purpose
"How long do you keep this data?"
A retention period per dataset tied to a purpose, enforced automatically.
Delete at the source, propagate to every derived store, crypto-shred immutable logs and backups.
Feedback loops and proxy bias: monitor outcomes per group, keep inputs for explanations.
Study notes on Designing Data-Intensive Applications, 2nd edition (Kleppmann & Riccomini). Read the book.
